children.name: Outcome 1.1 - By 2022, the people in Pakistan, especially the most vulnerable, marginalised and unskilled, benefit from improved inclusive and sustainable economic growth, progress towards full access to energy and fair trade practices.

Output 1.1.1 - Agricultural production strengthened through the rehabilitation of infrastructure; spearheading new technologies and modern production methods; by providing inputs and services, supporting the development of value chains while linking them to local and international markets
children.description:
UNIDO to establish a butchers training facility, and a model meat shop, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Food Safety and Halal Food Authority (KPFSHFA) and the Livestock and Dairy Development Department (LDD) food safety labs are being supported. An E-learning platform for Master Trainers has been developed on Good Hygiene Practice (GHP) as well as Good Animal Husbandry Practice (GAHP) for farmers and animal transporters. Upgradation of 30 butcher shops is currently underway.  Capacity building of government counterparts (LDD, KPFS&HFA & LCB) on new technique of dehiding thus improving quality of hides/skins for leather industry through Static Flaying Frame (SFF) and exposure to meat value chain.  Training and capacity building of private sector including feedlot farmers, butchers, meat exporters & processing industry on dehiding technique using SFF and animal/meat traceability.  Training of the private sector on the food safety and hygiene during slaughtering, evisceration, meat cuts, packing & packaging, storage and logistics in temperature controlled environment.  Understanding on feedlot farming business, farm management, preventive measures, animal buying and good husbandry practices to be adopted to improve meat quality and availability.  Initiation of a pilot project on animal and meat traceability starting from farm level through data management at all levels from buying till slaughtering, meat cuts, packaging and retail selling.  Exposure of meat value chain actors in understanding meat export business, International requirements, standards, approvals / certifications and quarantine protocols in meat export at an abattoir engaged in meat export.   Develop market linkages and exposure of private sector to understand high end market requirements and fulfil their food safety protocols and become partner in their economic activity/business. 
UNIDO upgraded and operationalized the only Pesticide Quality Control and Research Laboratory in Balochistan. 767 (358 female & 409 male) farmers have been trained on Good Agriculture Practices (GAP) in seven districts. An E-learning platform on GAP has also been developed for the agriculture department and farmers. The Balochistan PPP platform, established under the PAFAID project, regularly meets to ensure collaboration of stakeholders. The organization of the first-ever apple packaging solution competition among the students of key universities in Balochistan. Training of 17 food inspectors (16 male & 1 female) on “Risk-Based Food Inspection and Food Safety Management Systems” and Good Hygiene Practices from Balochistan Food Authority
Training of 29 (26 male and 3 female) stakeholders and  403 students (162 male and 241) on packaging solutions in collaboration with World Packaging Organization. Assessment of the four businesses/facilities to identify and support potential for capacity building, improved food safety practices and new value adding technologies for apple processing. The project has initiated a competition on the implementation of good agriculture practices among the apple farmers in the seven districts of Balochistan. The purpose of the competition is to assess the implementation the good agriculture practices by the farmers who were trained on GAP by the master trainers.

Output 1.1.5 - Strengthened capacities of public and private sector entities to implement policies and plans in the field of energy efficiency and renewable energy through promotion of new mechanisms for advancing solar, biomass and other renewable energy technologies, such as introducing business-to-business (B2B) models in the private sector
children.description:
Policy Recommendations for the promotion of Renewable Energy  & Energy Efficiency developed and handed over to NEECA and AEDB. Published reports on Sectoral Analysis of Energy Intensive Sectors and Analytical report to summarize the energy-saving data from all Energy Efficiency Interventions in 50 industrial sectors. A forward approach has been taken to cover energy assessments and the implementation of the EnMS based on ISO 50001-2018 in 50 selected industrial units. Overall 800+ different capacity-building trainings were conducted to enhance the knowledge and skills of professionals and young entrepreneurs which includes more than 100 young women energy professionals, trained in 20 different types of training stretched over one day to three days. Special grants were provided to 11 industrial units that were interested in ISO 5001 certification and needed financial push for energy optimization investments. 11 Industries have successfully completed the ISO 50001:2018 certification. Other industries are working on the implementation and certification of ISO 50001. Building the capacity of public and private sectors. During the implementation of EnMS, around 20 industry professionals have been trained and received lead auditor certifications on ISO 50001:2018. In the project’s concluding phase 11 Webinars and 4 Workshops were organized to disseminate learning of the projects related to EnMS and RE& EE to other industries that were not part of the project. A total of 12 success stories were drafted to highlight the impact of the project including the portfolio of implementation of EnMS/SO and deployment of RE. the document also illustrates the mandate of UNIDO i.e., Inclusive and Sustainable Industrial Development ensured across the project. Out of the 20 training, two specialized training sessions were on Certified Energy Manager (CEM) and Certified Energy Auditors (CEA). Special grants were provided to 11 industrial units that were interested in ISO 5001 certification and needed financial push for energy optimization investments.11 Industries have successfully completed the ISO 50001:2018 certification. Other industries are working on the implementation and certification of ISO 50001.Building the capacity of public and private sectors. During the implementation of EnMS, around 20 industry professionals have been trained and received lead auditor certifications on ISO 50001:2018. 
In the project’s concluding phase 11 Webinars and 4 Workshops were organized to disseminate learning of the projects related to EnMS and RE& EE to other industries that were not part of the project. A total of 12 success stories were drafted to highlight the impact of the project including the portfolio of implementation of EnMS/SO and deployment of RE. the document also illustrates the mandate of UNIDO i.e., Inclusive and Sustainable Industrial Development ensured across the project.  Upscaling RE investments in the industrial sector through developing partnerships with industries for implementing RE projects of a capacity of 12+ MWs for captive power purposes. Grants are provided for the implementation of RE projects in industries. 
6+ MW of Solar PV Projects have been completed based on the B2B model;
 5+ MW of PV captive power plants installed at different industrial units;
 1+ MW RE projects in support of small businesses and micro-enterprises including women-owned enterprises for productive uses;
Collaborated with the National Rural Support Program (NRSP) for Renewable Energy Investment Projects. UNIDO has achieved and exceeded the target, by installing 1.3 MW RE projects cumulatively instead of the target of 600 KW. That includes 474 beneficiaries together with 21 women-owned enterprises.
The Energy Desk has been established in collaboration with SMEDA with the prime objective to provide a one-window platform to facilitate the promotion of RE and EE technologies and investments in small and medium enterprises in Pakistan. The primary aim of the Energy Desk is to counsel and guide SMEs regarding the adoption of EE and RE technologies and provide information on market players including service providers, technology suppliers, financing facilities options, and regulatory updates. As a successful pilot scheme, UNIDO’s Energy Performance Awards have set a platform for a regular national-level event to motivate the industrial sector to contribute toward a sustainable, clean, and green Pakistan. Besides from an initiative taken by UNIDO by introducing AEE USA Certification courses like CEA and CEM at the local level, the professional who attended the courses, worked to set a  local chapter of the Association of Energy Engineers (AEE). UNIDO project team members, took active participation and also become key office holders (honorary basis) to align this chapter with project activities. The chapter is conducting regular webinars/training on RE/EE-related subjects and providing advisory services to local professional. 
USAID-funded PPSE is a dedicated Private Financing Advisory Network (PFAN) project in Pakistan to support Clean Energy Financing in Pakistan and Investment facilitation for clean energy projects enhanced by upstream and downstream activities. 
Project sourcing through local team, outreach events, partners and public stakeholders
46 projects on boarded and robust upcoming pipeline
Launched SME Accelerator for SMEs and Startups 
20 SMEs supported in SME Accelerator
14 Projects ready for investment facilitation

children.name: Outcome 4.1 - By 2022, children, adolescent girls and pregnant and lactating women have improved dietary intake and feeding and care practices, resulting in improved nutritional status, reducing stunting and other forms of under nutrition.

Output 4.1.1 - Integrated and multi-sectoral ‘National and Provincial Nutrition’ policies, strategies and initiatives are developed and implemented including enhanced public financial allocations in line with provincial priorities including sustained momentum of Scaling UP Nutrition (SUN) interventions across Pakistan.
children.description:
WFP provided technical support to SUN secretariat and SUN units in Balochistan and Sindh. Due to Nation wide emergency Nutrition markers  exercise is delayed in some areas. The process for the development of a costed multi sectoral national nutrition action plan with provincial roadmap contributed to increased capacity for planning, coordination, monitoring and strengthening of multi-sectoral nutrition programming. Public financing for nutrition remains a challenge, however some funds for the Accelerated Action Plan for stunting reduction programme (AAP) in Sindh, and Procurement of Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF) were allocated by the Government of  Sindh and Punjab Provinces.  

Coordination mechanisms and Technical Working Groups providing a platform for multisectoral coordination on Early Childhood Development were established in each province to engage across education, child protection, health, and nutrition sectors with support from UNICEF.    

Public financial allocation reviews are institutionalized for annual development plans through the SUN platform with UNICEF's technical support, to understand the level and division of financial allocation for nutrition-specific and -sensitive interventions in over one thousand public sector annual development plans in PAK, GB, Punjab and KP. Knowledge on public financial allocation is used to systematically advocate for increased investment in nutrition-sensitive interventions.

children.name: Output 4.1.2 - Current multi-sector nutrition strategies are implemented to improve dietary intake, feeding and care practices among vulnerable groups – including children, adolescent girls, pregnant and lactating women and mothers.
children.description: In 2022, evidence was generated with technical support from UNICEF for integrated packages of community health and nutrition services which increased cost-effectiveness in reaching families and communities by avoiding duplication of services and efforts. The trained 250 LHWs and Lady Health Supervisors are enabled to deliver messages on Immunization, nutrition, WASH, maternal, infant and young child nutrition, and key family care practices.

children.name: Output 4.1.3 - Nutrition-specific and nutrition-sensitive interventions are implemented with a focus on preventing and treating stunting, acute malnutrition, micronutrient deficiencies and maternal malnutrition.
children.description:
Nutrition sensitive social safety programme- BISP Nashonuma has been scaled up, so far 410 FC are operational 79 more will be established by end of February 2023. around 430,000 children under 2 and PLW received specialized nutritious food along with health and immunization services.
Integrated CMAM programme for the moderate malnutrition was implemented in 14 districts of KP and AJK. Around 78000 beneficiaries receives nutrition support.
WHO established 11 NSC in 2022 in Sindh and Balochistan, 38 NSCs strengthened across Pakistan and provided therapeutic milk to 11 New and 38 strengthened NSCs. In trainings on BFHI,  40 medical officers and 20 Nurses trained from Islamabad and KPK.

33.4 million children 6-59 months old were provided two doses of Vitamin A in 2022, with supply support from UNICEF.
Although there are large number of severly wasted children yet to be reached, a total of 323,032 children (146,176 boys and 176,856 girls) were admitted for treatment of severe wasting. Multiple micronutrient supplemention provided to 822,231 children (409,340 boys and 412,891 girls) and IFA supplementation to 1,789,507 mothers and 522,000 adolescent in 2022, for which UNICEF provided technical support in capacity building.             

Provincial implementation plans for the Maternal and Adolescent Nutrition Strategy were developed with UNICEF's support, and approved by provincial and national Governments. The strategy was lauched in Balochistan, Sindh and Gilgit-Balchistan, while launch in the remaining provinces and implementation will commence in 2023.

children.description:
Keeping in veiw the emerging nutrition needs
Nutrition flood emergency response was effectively coordinated through national, provincial and divisional/hub nutrition cluster platforms and  provided guidance to the nutrition emergency action in integerated manner.

The capacity of 250 Lady Health Workers on Nutrition is improved for providing quality nutrition services through the inclusion of nutrition into the Lady Health workers strategic and training documents.

children.description: A nutrition module for DHIS-2 was developed and rolled out in 4 districts with the support of UNICEF, which will improve the quality and nutrition information system. It will be rolled out to more districts in 2023. The nutrition commodities were integerated into the health information and mangment system to track the supplies at district and facility level.

children.description: To implement Nationally Determined Contributions in Pakistan UNDP completed nationwide provincial consultation (Punjab, Sindh, Baluchistan, AJK, KP and GB) and facilitated provinces and regions to identify priority actions to implement the NDC [EA 2.4.3 IRRF 1.1.1] (E66).  A policy paper was developed to unfold the potential of Blue Economy in the coastal areas of Pakistan and in this regard, the partnership with World Bank is being established [E78] [IRRF]. UNDP enhanced the capacity of provincial disaster management authorities Sindh and Balochistan in development and dissemination of national school safety guide for earthquake and tsunamis. The regional school safety guidelines have been considered a benchmark to develop a context-based framework for Pakistan. The guidelines will strengthen community-level preparedness and response against the coastal hazards [E79] [IRRF 1.1.1].

children.description: To implement Nationally Determined Contributions in Pakistan UNDP completed nationwide provincial consultation (Punjab, Sindh, Baluchistan, AJK, KP and GB) and facilitated provinces and regions to identify priority actions to implement the NDC [EA 2.4.3 IRRF 1.1.1] (E66). The guidelines will strengthen community-level preparedness and response against the coastal hazards [E79] [IRRF 1.1.1].  Likewise,for enhanced resilience of tsunami prone coastal areas of Pakistan UNDP undertook multiple policy level interventions such as earthquake  and tsunami risk assessment of coastal belt of Karachi, development of Tsunami early warning communication and dissemination SOPs, earthquake and tsunami guidelines for implanting tsunami building bylaws and codes for coastal areas and risk reduction policy framework for tsunami and earthquake [E80-80.3] [IRRF 3.1.2].UNDP supported to provincial and districts disaster management authorities to strengthen 19 buildings (13 schools, and 6 health facilities) through retrofitting to demonstrate sustainability and financial efficacy of structural mitigation measures for any event like earthquakes, tsunamis, and cyclones [E81][IRRF 3.1.2].Furthermore, the project is constructing 14 tsunami evacuation sites (designated areas with shelter facilities), preparing, and marking evacuation routes with tsunami signboards following regional and global best practices in Malir and Keamari districts in Sindh and Gwadar in Balochistan [E10] [IRRF 3.1.2].

children.description: In order to generate more employment across various sectors, a new Economic Development Plan for KP was developed by UNDP, which has now been approved by the KP Chief Minister [E70].Further, in an effort to decrease unemployment, UNDP trained 2,480 youth (men 1,696 and women 784) in different industrial trades, 223 (men 151, women 72) in eco-tourism e-commerce, and another 410 (men 243, women 159, transgenders 8) in social entrepreneurs under SDG bootcamp funded by JAZZ [E71]. Out of these, 1,238 (boys 866, girls 372) are working [E72]. In collaboration with the KP Tourism Department, UNDP trained, 210 youths (68 women) around Eco Tourism and E-Commerce (Dir and Swat) where potential for E-commerce and Eco Tourism is imminent [E73IRRF3.3.1]. UNDP in Balochistan enhanced the capacity of marginalized youth (280 including 90 women) and trained them in different technical and vocational trades enhancing the potential of Small-Scale Supplier [E74][IRRF3.3.1]. To enhance economic growth opportunities, UNDP initiated process for increasing access of Medium, Small, and Micro Entrepreneurs (MSMEs) and youth in North Waziristan, South Waziristan, and Khyber district to formal financing. UNDP (through its responsible party; iConsult) has started engagement with potential commercial banks to extend their services in the project districts and develop products that could attract the MSMEs and youth for business purpose [E75][EA2.2.1].Under WASH IWP priority area, to support the Balochistan Government, UNDP initiated renovation and repair work of hospitals and schools in 2 districts (Nushki and Killa Abdullah) and five out of 29 schemes (schools and hospitals) have been completed [E69.1][IRRF3.2.2].  In KP, for improved livelihood, construction and rehabilitation of WASH services in 82 market hubs and 02 water filtration plants were initiated [E76], with an aim to bring more clients to the markets.

children.description:
For protection of people especially in the northern zones prone to natural hazards UNDP enhanced the capacity of national and provincial disaster management authorities through formulation of several policies and actions plans related to climate change and adaptation and disaster risk reduction (DRR). This included updating of National Climate Change Policy (draft in 2021), Nationally determined Contributions (NDCs) (2021), and Climate Change Action Plans at the provincial level (2021). In collaboration with Capital Development Authority, Under the waste management initiative, 19,371 people (including 9104 women) got access to improved waste management system in two sectors of Islamabad. 200 sanitary staff (35 women, 165 men) received training on waste collection and segregation, 33 sets (120 Litres bins) of 3 bins system were also installed and 51 yellow-colored bins were also distributed in the target sectors. During the year, 5 low-cost plastic recycling solutions were also formulated by different academic institutions through UNESCO and the Pakistan Science Foundation to transform plastic into products like plastic and filaments that can be used in 3D printers. UNDP also provided 45 benches made from recycled plastics and handed over these benches to Capital Development Authority and Senate of Pakistan[E83][IRRF 4.1.1].

Further UNDP’s capacity building initiatives enabled the district disaster response teams to conduct independent early recovery needs assessments of early recovery of people in emergency. UNDP assisted the governments of Sindh and KP to save people from risks of climate change through formulating landscape management plans. Similarly with the same aim it aided the government of KP by providing a management information system for forest monitoring resulting in effective forest management.   
In 2022, for enhanced climate resilience of people of Pakistan, UNDP supported development and finalization of two Climate Change Adaptation Action Plans (CCAAPs) for GB and KP, which have been adopted by the respective provincial Governments and being used to address and mitigate GLOF risks and adverse impacts of climate change. 
For effective disaster preparedness and mitigation of public at large, KP and GB has been supported by UNDP to develop four plans (02 monsoon and 02 winter contingency) [E65-E65.5][EA 4.2.3]. 
In 2021, with support of UNDP Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) were updated and submitted to UNFCCC by the government of Pakistan.

children.name: Output 6.1.7 - Disaster prone communities enabled to better anticipate and cope with natural calamities related to the climate change
children.description: Likewise, for enhanced resilience of tsunami prone coastal areas of Pakistan UNDP undertook multiple policy level interventions such as earthquake and tsunami risk assessment of coastal belt of Karachi, development of Tsunami early warning communication and dissemination SOPs, earthquake and tsunami guidelines for implanting tsunami building bylaws and codes for coastal areas and risk reduction policy framework for tsunami and earthquake [E80-80.3] [IRRF 3.1.2].UNDP supported to provincial and districts disaster management authorities to strengthen 19 buildings (13 schools, and 6 health facilities) through retrofitting to demonstrate sustainability and financial efficacy of structural mitigation measures for any event like earthquakes, tsunamis, and cyclones [E81][IRRF 3.1.2].Furthermore, the project is constructing 14 tsunami evacuation sites (designated areas with shelter facilities), preparing, and marking evacuation routes with tsunami signboards following regional and global best practices in Malir and Keamari districts in Sindh and Gwadar in Balochistan [E10] [IRRF 3.1.2].In consultation with Met office and GBDMA, UNDP installed 04 Automated Weather Stations (01 each) in Passu, Gulkin, Shisper and Askole in [E09][IRRF 3.1.2] GB. AWS restoration survey on Baltoro region from Askole to Concordia was completed as well as multi-temporal and field analysis of 04 glaciers and glacial bodies were conducted [E9]. National Met office is being taken on board as Procurement of additional 24 EWS for GB is now complete. Once it is installed, will benefit 100 percent population of 24 valleys to cope with potential disaster of GLOF (IRRF 3.1.2) [E78]. For supporting marginalized people UNDP through line departments in GB and KP built 67 small scale infrastructure, which are benefiting 44,702 people (Men: 21,567, women 23,135), and 55 irrigation channels benefiting 13,210 people (Men 6,570, women 6,640) in 24 project valleys. 400hectare slope stabilization activities have been completed in 2022, which have enabled area to be brought under sustainable forest management [E82][IRRF4.1.2].

Output 6.1.6: Integrated post-disaster recovery support that restores living conditions and reduces vulnerability to future shocks (IOM).
children.description: IOM through its Ips, implemented the Flood Emergency Response in Sindh carried out a detailed Early Recovery Needs Assessment (ERNA) from 01 to 20 November 2020 in districts Mirpurkhas, Umerkot and Sanghar to plan for recovery interventions and identify remaining gaps in the response phase. The assessment findings showed that there were unmet needs for the provision of shelter assistance, including repairing or rebuilding damaged shelters; rehabilitation and installation of WASH facilities with major focus on water for drinking and other uses, complemented by hygiene promotion for safe hygienic practices; and need for assistance in restoration of their well-being through livelihood and income generating activities. Based on these findings, IOM planned and proposed a 3.5 month long Early Recovery Intervention in the districts of Dadu, Mirpurkhas, Sajawal, Sanghar, Tando Muhammad Khan and Umerkot, starting from 15 December 2020 till 31 March 2021.

framework.name: Strategic Priority 8 - Gender Equality and Rights

children.name: Outcome 8.1 - By 2022, government institutions will have increased accountability towards gender equality commitments and social, economic, cultural and political rights.

Output 8.1.1 - Provision of support to legal and policy reforms that are gender-sensitive and responsive, particularly related to HIV, SRH, women’s empowerment, gender-based violence and discrimination.
Output 8.1.2 - Implementation of Action Plans to raise women’s and minorities’ participation in decision making, cultural expression and key sectors like the media.

Output 8.1.3 - Strengthened capacities for monitoring of gender-responsive frameworks and progress on issues like food and nutrition security, the social determinants of health and health equity including development of systems, benchmarks and research to generate data on human rights- and gender-related SDG and CEDAW indicators.

Output 8.1.4 - Strengthened institutional mechanisms for human rights and gender equality, while advocating for a specific mechanism – within and among government departments – to accelerate progress on cross-cutting issues in each socio-economic sector.

Output 8.1.5 - Assisting federal and provincial counterparts to enhance access to quality multi-sectoral sexual and reproductive health services and rights – spanning health care, justice, policing and safe spaces – while advocating for the integration of gender concerns into all health planning, policies and programmes.

Output 8.1.6 - Promoting a coordinated, effective response to GBV across all sectors, including justice & health systems including initiatives to prevent and address GBV & discrimination against women, girls and transgender persons as well as specific solutions for vulnerable groups like Afghan refugees & TDPs to secure their sustainable reintegration.

Output 8.1.7 - Strengthening the knowledge & capacities of law enforcement agencies, criminal justice institutions, decision makers, opinion leaders and multiple service delivery sectors – health, WASH, nutrition and education – on human rights and gender equality.

Output 8.1.8 - Promoting positive, public narratives around religious and social tolerance, as well as gender equality, to elicit and sustain positive behavioral change including measures aimed at addressing prevalent social norms around gender and gender stereotyping.
Output 8.1.9 - Gender sensitization and integration of gender inclusive interventions in climate resilient agriculture, disaster risk reduction programming

Outcome 9.1 - By 2022, the people in Pakistan, especially the most vulnerable and marginalized, have increased knowledge of their rights and improved access to more accountable, transparent and effective governance mechanisms and rule of law institutions.

Output 9.1.1 - Democratic governance of 'State' institutions, including 'Parliament', 'Provincial Assemblies', 'Local Governments' and 'Electoral Management Bodies' (EMBs) strengthened to be transparent, accountable and responsive to citizens' needs for improved service delivery (UNDP/UNODC)
children.description:
UNDP undertook national level voter education campaign for enhanced awareness of public for upcoming general elections. UNDP support to Election Commission of Pakistan comprised of technical and professional skills of 1,377 officers (1160 men, 217 women) 21 ECP officers (19 men 3 women) [E33]; testing and development of elections monitoring system [E34]; support for research and development structure, staffing plan, draft roadmap for Internet Voting System (IVS)[E35]. To ensure free and fair elections, UNDP educated youth voters (3,237=1,683 women and 1,554 men) in universities, and colleges while 1,163 stakeholders (37 women and 1,126 men) were engaged through sessions held with media, local communities, Civil Society in KP, Balochistan[E18]. UNDP supported voter education campaigns through multiple media sources for Local Government Elections in KP (18.181m reached for phase II), Balochistan (6.8m) and Sindh (44.03m) [E18][EA1.1.1].

To support parliament in election reforms act 2017, UNDP arranged extensive consultations (amendment bill 2021). The bill has reached for debate in the Parliament [E36] [IRRF 2.4.1EA 1.1.1]. 

 UNDP has supported over 40 stakeholder engagements of Home and Tribal Affairs Department (HTAD) KP and district administrations which led to improved service delivery mechanisms in merged area border communities [E32.1-E32.4][IRRF 1.1.1]. UNDP’s explored key factors behind delayed recruitment for top-level vacancies (Executive Recruitment in Public Sector Organizations) and developed a recruitment manual for Ministry to expedite their recruitment process. 

For improved health service delivery, UNDP supported the national and provincial AIDS control programmers (ACPs), to treat HIV positive patients (16,782 women 45,470 men) with anti-retroviral therapy (ART) against HIV [E08][IRRF1.4.1].

children.name: Output 9.1.2 - Efficiency, effectiveness and responsiveness of the 'Rule of Law' institutions improved for timely, affordable and accessible provision of justice services (UNDP/UNODC/UNWOMEN,UNICEF)
children.description:
With UNDP’s support Merged Areas’ have their first ever Policing Plans [E40-E40.7] [IRRF2.2.1] for effective law enforcement in the area. KP police has a public outreach strategy which is helping KP Police to know it’s public perception and positioning[E41][IRRF2.2.1].Women participation in provincial legal profession in KP, has been encouraged through UNDP’s stipends and scholarships for law students [E42] [IRRF2.2.3: EA 1.2.1]. 

Through provision of 35 virtual courts and 75 virtual points and linking of Peshawar High Court through this facility with prisons has increased the case disposal rate [E43][IRRF2.2.3EA 1.2.1]. To make informal justice mechanisms more efficient in KP/MAs, UNDP supported the revision of Dispute Resolution Councils (DRC) Rules under KP Police Act 2017 [E44] and for formal justice mechanisms included technical support to Balochistan High Court for development of court-annexed mediation rules under section 89-A, Civil Procedure Court 1908, to ensure simpler and affordable legal solutions for the people [E45][IRRF2.2.1]
With support of UNDP, Balochistan judiciary has operational ADR mechanism and adopted courts annexed rules under section 89-A [E46]. Whereas KP has revised ‘KP Prison and Act rules’ while leading to improved conditions of the inmates[E47-E48-E49][IRRF 2.2.1]. 

With UNDP’s support Peshawar based KP Forensic Science Laboratory was operationalized and Service and Operations Rules under the 2020 Act were developed [E25] a great step towards speedy prosecution investigations in the province. 

UNDP enhanced access to justice through establishing the Provincial Justice Committee (PJC) Secretariate at PHC which is closely coordinating with the District Criminal Justice Coordination Committees (CJCCs) [IRRF 2.2.1]. UNDP supported Ministry of Human Rights in developing a strategy for harmonizing human rights data collection mechanisms [E51] while complementing the implementation of Pakistan’s National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights.

children.name: Output 9.1.3 - Through active citizens engagement, public policy priorities shaped by national/provincial governments, planning, financing and monitoring mechanisms established, statistical capacities of core governing institutions strengthened, facilitating implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals (UNDP/UNFPA/UNHABITAT/UNICEF/WHO)
children.description:
UNDP’s technical support to the government to shape priority policy areas continued in 2022. 

A joint ‘SDG Investment Report 2021’ was published in partnership with the government on Financing for Development and nature capital solutions [E54][EA1.3.1]. Additionally following interventions were undertaken such as portfolio presentations at global investment platforms such as the SDG Investment Fairs and ESCAP’s Asia Pacific Forum [E55][EA1.3.1]; launch of the SDG Investments and Climate Financing Facility, development of high-impact SDG-aligned value propositions for private sector investment [E06] [EA1.3.1]. A diagnostic report on Inclusive Insurance and Risk Financing in Pakistan was published [E56]; countrywide consultations on Disaster Risk Financing solutions [E57] have created buy-in from the Balochistan and Sindh governments to develop Insurance and Risk Financing solutions in their provinces [E58 and E58.1] [E.A 1.1.1]. 
Gender Training Assessments resulted in capacity-building trainings for government stakeholders all over Pakistan [E60]. To improve planning under SDG localization efforts, UNDP prepared frameworks for key priority sectors like social protection, health, and education at the sub-national level, such as district development plans and SDG frameworks, as well as documentation and Situation Analysis Reports on SDG 2, 4, 6 and 7 [E62][E.A 1.3.2] serving as baseline for future planning. UNDP has increased the citizens engagement by engaging the academia on the topic “Reimagining Resilience: the Transition to Sustainable Cities” [E16], and a report was also jointly launched on 'Migration, Livelihoods & Resilience in Karachi: A Study on Social Cohesion and Informal Urban Settlements' [E64].
